errorCodes.meaning: The typed number does not match. The request is declined.
The prove is not signed by the request's lock key.
The decision window has passed, or the request has otherwise ended.
The carried identify failed verification, does not match the request or the lock, or its issuer is not an active member. Deliberately generic. The request is declined.
The approver's network has hit the service's prove limit. `details.retryAfter` MAY give seconds until a retry.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

OobKey.description: A starter key (`K_b`) or an approver lock key (`K_a`), as an Ed25519 `did:key` (`z6Mk…`) generated for this one request and used nowhere else. Ed25519 only: a service refuses any other key type with `auth/oob:keyUnsupported` before parsing beyond the multicodec prefix.
OobKey.title: OobKey

Origin.description: A web origin (`https://host[:port]`, no path, no trailing slash) — for `login`, the origin of the portal where the starter runs, which is the origin of the `serviceEndpoint` of the service's `SignInPortal` service in its DID document.
Origin.title: Origin

Purpose.description: What the request is for. A CLOSED list: each purpose has a fixed row in CONVENTIONS.md §3 stating what is revealed at each step, what the grant contains, what redeem returns and the window lengths. Version 0.1 defines `login` only. `stepUp` and `deviceEnrol` are reserved names; adding one is a new version of this component and of every task that references it, never an in-place edit.
Purpose.title: Purpose

RequestId.description: The service-generated handle of one request: 16 to 32 bytes from a cryptographically secure random source, written as unpadded base64url (22 to 43 characters; 16 bytes, 22 characters, is RECOMMENDED). It is also the nonce of the exchange, so the family needs no separate challenge, and it is the `_id` of the trigger link (VTI-LNK-033). Compared as a string. It confers no authority on its holder.
RequestId.title: RequestId

Requester.description: What the service reports about where the request came from. Revealed only in the step 2 response, to the lock holder, after a membership and number proof. Reported by the service, signed by it, and a heuristic: a relaying attacker controls what is observed.

browser.description: Browser family of the starter (e.g. `Chrome`), never the full User-Agent; `unknown` when it cannot be told.

createdAt.description: When the service accepted the starter's auth/oob/request.

location.description: City and country of the starter's connection, from a local lookup with no third-party call, or the literal `unknown`. Never an IP address.

os.description: Operating system family of the starter (e.g. `macOS`); `unknown` when it cannot be told.

Requester.title: Requester

Response.description: Step 2 of the disclosure ladder, signed by the service's assertionMethod key: the step 1 members unchanged, plus the starter's key, where the request came from, which DID was identified and, optionally, the task families the starter key would sign for. The SHA-256 of its JCS canonical form, proof included, is the grant's `contextDigest`.

decisionClosesAt.description: Unchanged from step 1 (auth/oob/claim/0.2): when the decision window closes, as an RFC 3339 date-time.

identifiedAs.description: The DID that issued the verified identify document. A grant must come from this DID.

sessionKey.description: The starter key `K_b`: the key a grant would let act as the identified DID.

signingScope.description: The task families the service offers to let the starter key sign for, as `identifiedAs`, for the session a grant would arm (auth/oob/grant/0.3). Fixed by the service for the surface at `origin`. Absent: the grant delegates no signing.

Response.title: Auth — OOB Prove — response payload (step 2)

SameNetwork.description: Whether the starter's request and the approver's prove came from the same egress network, as the service saw them: `true`, `false`, or the string `unknown` when the service cannot tell. The service compares addresses; it never discloses them.
SameNetwork.title: SameNetwork

Service.description: Who the service says it is.

did.description: The service's DID: the `recipient` of every request in the family, and the `_from` of the trigger link.

name.description: The name the service calls itself. Supplied by the service: an approver shows the name from its OWN records and flags a difference from this one (VTI-LNK-104); it never shows this value as the community's name on its own authority.

Service.title: Service

SigningScope.description: The task families a `login` grant lets the starter key sign documents for, as the approving DID, for the session the grant arms (auth/oob/grant/0.2). Offered by the service in step 2, copied unchanged into the grant, and bounded further by the exclusions auth/oob/grant/0.2 states. Absent means the starter key signs nothing beyond the family's own tasks.
SigningScope.title: SigningScope

TaskFamily.description: A family of Trust Tasks, named by a slug prefix of whole segments (SPEC §6.1 grammar): `vtc/directory` names every task whose slug is `vtc/directory` or begins `vtc/directory/`, at any version. A prefix matches on segment boundaries only, so `vtc/dir` names nothing under `vtc/directory`.
TaskFamily.title: TaskFamily

schema.description: The lock holder proves membership and the number on the starter's screen by carrying a signed auth/oob/identify document, and gets back the service-signed step 2. Issued and signed by the lock key `K_a`. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, parentThreadId, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

identify.description: A complete, signed auth/oob/identify/0.1 Trust Task document, issued by the approving DID and signed by its VTA for `authentication`. The service verifies it as a document in its own right — envelope, proof and payload against that specification's schema — over the members exactly as received: its proof covers every member, so it is deliberately an open object here rather than a typed one a binding could narrow.

schema.title: Auth — OOB Prove — payload
